dct_description_sm: Research conducted by the Labrador Highlands Research Group on the climate and ecology of the Mealy Mountains has been ongoing since 2001.  One of the main goals of this research is to come away with a multidisciplinary understanding of treeline dynamics.  This knowledge will be combined as inputs for a climate-vegetation model being produced at Memorial University.  The purpose of this specific project is to examine the role that seed productivity and pre-dispersal seed limitation may play in these dynamics.  Seed cone production of four conifer species (black spruce, white spruce, eastern larch and balsam fir) and two shrub species (mountain alder and dwarf birch) was examined in different habitat types within the treeline region.  The productivity of seed cones by these species was evaluated in lower elevation closed canopy sites, higher open canopy sites, and above the treeline in tree islands and krummholz.  As increasing amounts of growing degree-days received can inhibit embryo maturation, seed viability will be examined with respect to the heat sum received at these different elevations and habitats.  Growing degree-day data will be taken from previously established climate stations within the mountains.  The role of predispersal seed loss to invertebrate predators and disease will also be evaluated through the inspection of sampled seed cones.  This study will therefore provide data on the viable seed contribution/unit area of a given species to the surrounding environment.
dct_title_s: Seed cone productivity in various habitat types within tree line dynamics in the Mealy Mountains, Labrador (2007-2008)
